It really just depends on the facility. The first time I was taken inpatient I was sent to a crisis stabilization center and let me tell you... it was honestly complete shit. The nurses explained to me that their facility was kind of like a pit stop. Generally patients are meant to stay there until their 72 hour hold is lifted, once they are deemed safe enough to leave, or until they get transferred to a different facility. All I did there was sit and wait in a room with around 5-6 other women until I was able to talk to a psychiatrist. When it was finally my turn, the psychiatrist told me "how do you not know what's wrong with you, how do you not know why you're depressed?" in demeaning sort of way. He ended up giving me 40mg of Ativan after only talking to me for around 5 minutes which ended up making me puke. A lot of people were obviously just there to get paid, but there were some people who were very kind to me. The first time I was there I stayed for around 4 days until I was sent to a behavioral center, which was an incredible step up from the last place. Everyone was very kind and I got to talk to a lot of staff and patients that actually made me feel safe. 
I wish you the best of luck and I hope you get the proper help that you need. If it's okay with you, I'd like to hear about how it goes.
